title: Span Economics — Weekly Lab Notes (tracing / dashboards / cost telemetry)
content:
TL;DR:
We ran the first week of the "Span Economics" micro-experiments: reduced high-cardinality span attributes, enabled strategic sampling on long-running calls, and deployed a lightweight dashboard that correlates span volume with cost buckets. Early signals: 12% reduction in trace ingestion volume for the GGP model pool, but a subtle uptick in missed error-context (2 incidents where spans lacked the debug_id field). We need to iterate on attribute truncation and add a fallback path for critical error fields.

Attendees / context:
- Raina (owner), Diego (sampling workstream), Amina (dashboards + billing metrics), Tobias (collector / ingestion)
- Standup cadence: weekly sync + asynchronous notes in #obs-span-econ.

What we did this week:
1) Sampling experiment alpha (INF-OBS-SAMP-A):
   - Enabled head-based sampling at 15% for requests > 4s to avoid full KV cache blowout from tail-heavy requests.
   - Introduced deterministic sampling key (customer_id hashed) so we can rehydrate for canary traffic.
   - Observed: tail latency traces dropped 8% in total span count for the targeted routes; throughput of the topology-ingest pipeline improved marginally (approx 6% fewer batch flushes).

2) Attribute reduction trial:
   - Truncated free-form "user_agent_extra" and removed duplicated routing metadata from span tags for the inference-serving path.
   - Observed: avg span size reduced from ~2.4KB -> 1.9KB; ingestion cost for that tag bucket moved from ~22% -> 17% of the span payload cost.

3) Dashboard MVP deployed:
   - New dashboard: "Span Economics — live" (few panels): span rate by service, median span size, ingestion cost by tag, and lost-debug-context counter (we track how often critical fields are absent).
   - Dashboard notes: we intentionally kept panels lightweight (no >10s heavy queries) to avoid incurring extra cost while debugging.

Signals & anomalies observed:
- GGP pool: 12% lower span ingestion (good), but 2 postmortems flagged missing debug_id in error spans (bad). Root cause appears to be attribute truncation and an env var ordering issue in the SDK that caused debug_id to be populated in a higher-level tag that we trimmed.
- Spike on 2026-07-29 09:12 UTC: sudden 40% rise in span count for internal-batcher due to a retry storm originating from infra change (INF-DEPLOY-817). Happened ~20 minutes before autoscaling corrected the upstream queue.
- Cost delta estimate: projected monthly ingestion savings if current configs persisted: ~$3.2k (approx 9% of ingestion spend for tracing). This is preliminary and requires invoice reconciliation.

Hypotheses to test next week:
- H1: Reintroducing a small dedicated "error_context" tag (<=128 bytes) will recover the missing debug_id without increasing costs significantly. Test by toggling on for 25% of error traces (sampled by error code + deterministic customer key).
- H2: Adaptive sampling (heat-based) will reduce budget overruns more than static head-based sampling. Plan a two-week A/B on internal-batcher route (A: static 15%, B: heat-adaptive target throughput 10-15%).

Planned experiments & rough plan:
- Experiment EE-2 (7/31 deploy): implement error_context tag and monitor lost-debug-context counter + error-rate delta for 72h.
- Experiment EE-3 (8/3 start): lightweight adaptive sampler prototype in the OTEL collector; metrics: span volume, ingestion latency, critical-field-loss. Run for 14 days, stop early if customer-impacting data is missing.

Dashboard / alert changes to land:
- Alert: lost-debug-context > 0.5% over 1h (new) --> pager to oncall + annotate rollout. Ticket created OBS-4219.
- Panel: span-size P90 by service (to detect regressions after SDK changes).
- Cost panel: ingestion cost by tag bucket with 7d rolling window (Amina will help model the mapping to billing SKU).

Open implementation notes / chores:
- Tobias: add fallback that forces debug_id into error_context when present but missing from main attributes (INF-OBS-390).
- Diego: add deterministic sampling flag to the collector so we can fully rehydrate samples for a single customer on-demand. Needs PR and release notes (PR draft: #212).
- Raina/Amina: reconcile billing estimate with finance next week to validate the $3.2k projection (add to agenda for Fri finance sync).

Risks / tradeoffs discussed:
- Risk of losing critical debug info vs. cost savings. Mitigation: narrow attribute truncation to only known high-entropy fields; add a small, non-optional error payload for all error spans.
- Risk of sampler biasing metrics (A/B to detect). We will wire additional guard rails in dashboards to surface metric drifts (e.g., request-success-by-sampled-vs-raw).

Quick wins / small todo list:
- Roll back truncation for 'routing_trace_id' until fallback is in place (immediate).
- Add a short runbook for debugging 'lost-debug-context' incidents in the repo (2 person-hours).
- Add sample-rate metadata to the trace root so dashboards can segment metrics by effective_sample_rate.

Questions for next sync / decisions required:
- Do we want to baseline adaptive sampling per-service or at the collector cluster level? (tradeoff: per-service is more precise but operationally heavier).
- How aggressive do we want truncation to be on customer-provided metadata? Default: conservative (only trim fields we know are high-entropy).

Notes to self:
- Keep running the 15% head-sample for long routes for one more week to collect steady-state.
- Prepare a 5-slide summary for infra sync on Friday focusing on 1) cost delta, 2) incidents prevented/caused, 3) recommended rollout path.

Relevant tickets & links (quick):
- OBS-4213: Span Economics alpha plan
- OBS-4219: lost-debug-context alert
- INF-DEPLOY-817: retry storm incident
